problem: For the function $g(x,y,z)=\sqrt{x}\operatorname{arccos}⁡(y{z}^{2}),$ evaluate $\frac{∂g}{∂z}$ at the point $(3,\frac{1}{2},1).$
worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $z,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the constant multiple and chain rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\sqrt{x}\operatorname{arccos}⁡(y{z}^{2})) \\  & =\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡(y{z}^{2})) \\  & =\sqrt{x}\cdot (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{(y{z}^{2})}^{2}}})\cdot \frac{∂}{∂z}(y{z}^{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{x}\cdot (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}{z}^{4}}})\cdot y\cdot 2z \\  & =-\frac{2yz\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}{z}^{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(3,\frac{1}{2},1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂z}{|}_{(3,\,1/2,\,1)} & =-\frac{2(\frac{1}{2})(1)\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{1-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}(1)^{4}}} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{4}}} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$
